articles.title: 'Carrick is going to be gone by Christmas'
articles.summary: The co-host of the Devil's Advocate podcast, Gaz Drinkwater, believes the "writing is on the wall" for Michael Carrick and that the former Manchester United...
articles.body:
The co-host of the Devil's Advocate podcast, Gaz Drinkwater , believes the "writing is on the wall" for Michael Carrick and that the former Manchester United midfielder will be sacked by Christmas.

After five league matches, United sit 12th in the table on five points - their joint-worst return at this stage of a Premier League season.

A late Matheus Cunha equaliser helped spare Carrick's blushes against Fulham and avoided United going into the long international break on the back of three straight defeats in all competitions.

This run included getting knocked out of the Carabao Cup in embarrassing fashion when they let a two-goal lead slip against Brighton at Old Trafford - plus a home derby defeat by Manchester City.

However, even though Drinkwater believes it would be "reckless" to call time on Carrick's tenure in charge already, he thinks that outcome is inevitable.

"Obviously Michael Carrick hasn't done enough to get sacked," he said. "I'm not saying that. Sacking him now would be trigger-happy, would be reckless and would be silly.

"You have to judge him over at the very least 10 games of the Premier League season.

"The writing is on the wall already. He's going to be gone by Christmas. He's not going to turn this around. He's going to be gone by Christmas, so what's the point in him being here now?

"It doesn't fix anything, by the way. I don't think it's going to be a Ruben Amorim situation where the new guy comes in and he actually does sensible things. I don't necessarily think that's the case this time.

"I was watching it [against Fulham ] and it's like the players don't look very good. The quality isn't there. The passing was ridiculous. Loose touches, horrible football. I hope he turns it around."

articles.title: 'We deserve to win something - this could be the year'
articles.summary: Joe: This may read as a bizarre statement as a lifelong fan - I do not want Brighton to win any silverware this year.  Having said that, I'd hope Tony Bloom...
articles.body:
We asked for your views on what Brighton can achieve this season after the Seagulls beat Arsenal 3-0 to climb up to third in the Premier League, with 10 points from their opening five matches.

Steve: Obviously we need to stay grounded but if we can have a season not being a feeder club we could achieve something amazing and then we can attract the established big names to keep us fighting for the top six year after year. We deserve to win something and this could be the year.

Joe: This may read as a bizarre statement as a lifelong fan - I do not want Brighton to win any silverware this year. A highly entertaining season playing attractive football? Yes please. Winning silverware? No thanks. It'll just give the club an excuse to put prices up across the board as evidenced by the 'big' clubs. Having said that, I'd hope Tony Bloom would be better than that if a trophy arrives, which I'm sure he is.

Nicholas: Brighton have set the bar for other clubs. Well run and able to find diamonds that other clubs can't. Next step is strengthening for Europe. This season will be a test of how far the club has come. Chants of "seagulls pecking" might become a regular occurrence.

Matthew: The Albion are better placed than any of the previous two seasons under Hurzeler to achieve "something special" this season, perhaps that elusive trophy, or a second top-six finish. The sky is the limit for this squad, which is now deeper than ever, ruthlessly dismantling the champions despite numerous injuries to key players.

So why should we be cautious before getting too excited? After the long momentum-sapping international break we have our first run of European games either side of Premier League games that will provide no respite.

The fading light plus wind, rain and dropping temperatures have in the past two seasons been accompanied by fading form and frustration from fans. Whether we can better navigate the winter months and rotate our squad effectively will determine whether this season will be a special one.

Simon: If these levels of performance are maintained, that is a 76-point season! Is this achievable? Or can it be bettered? Who knows...

articles.title: Oklahoma's David Stone suffers knee injury in Monday's practice as 'it kind of popped out'
articles.summary: Stone entered the 2026 season as a potential first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
Oklahoma could be without star defensive lineman David Stone on Saturday against No. 2 Georgia. Stone suffered a knee injury during practice on Monday.

After a report said that Stone was injured while playing offense during practice, coach Brent Venables on Tuesday made clear that Stone was not on that side of the ball when the injury occurred and one of his knees "kind of popped out."

"David Stone, I know it was reported that he was hurt last night at practice, he wasn't on offense, I guess that was out there — he was on offense," Venables said at his news conference. "But he wasn't on offense when he got banged up. He ran his knee into a scout team player during a jog through and it kind of popped out. We'll see where he's at. The X-rays were positive, I guess. I'm reporting the news. That's all I'm doing, reporting the news. But he said his pain was about a two out of 10 right now and so we'll kind of go from there."

Venables wouldn't comment on Stone's status for Saturday's game or any potential long-term absence and said Stone's game status would be reflected on Oklahoma's Wednesday injury report.

"If David is unavailable this week, we're going to need some guys to step up and play big," Venables said.

Stone is a potential first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft who was slated to take on a bigger role up front for the Sooners in 2026. He has 12 tackles, two tackles for loss and a half sack through Oklahoma's first three games of the season. In 2025, Stone had 42 total tackles, 8 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks.

The Sooners are 2-1 after losing to Michigan in Week 2 and enter Saturday's game as a 14-point underdog after scoring just 14 points in an eight-point win over New Mexico in Week 3.

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Nations League 'a great opportunity' for NI - Dan Ballard
articles.summary: Northern Ireland defender Dan Ballard says the squad have "a lot of talent and hunger" ahead of their Nations League quadruple-header.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland defender Dan Ballard said the squad have "a lot of talent and hunger" as they prepare for their tough Nations League quadruple-header.

Ballard is back on the international stage after missing April's World Cup play-off semi-final defeat by Italy and June's friendlies against Guinea and France due to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old has impressed for Sunderland this campaign and, after a frustrating spell on the sidelines, is excited for the chance to pull on a green shirt again.

"It is a great opportunity for some of the lads who haven't got as many minutes as there will defo be opportunities this camp," Ballard told BBC Sport NI.

"There are some new faces and young faces who we are really excited to see come through.

"Sometimes we forget how strong a squad we have and then you look at training and there are a lot of hungry players who want to be involved. We have a lot of work to do, but there is a lot of talent and hunger."

Due to a change in the international schedule, Northern Ireland will now play four matches this window for the first time since 2022.

Michael O'Neill's side travel to face Georgia on 25 September and welcome Hungary three days later before a trip to Slovakia to face Ukraine and a home match against Georgia on 5 October.

Despite having to balance four games in just an 11-day span, Ballard believes the side will be ready.

"The lads are now experienced enough, a lot of play in the Championship and league one and there are a lot of games," he continued.

"I am lucky enough to be playing in Europe this year [with Sunderland], so we have to get used to it. I think these four games will be really good for us.

"The games are coming thick and fast and we just have to do everything we can to prepare. It is tough on the mind and on our bodies, but we love playing games and that is why we do it. I am sure we will be ready."

articles.title: El Albacete iguala su peor arranque en lo que va de siglo
articles.standfirst: La temporada 2007-2008 empezó igual, perdió en la séptima jornada, cambió de entrenador en febrero y acabó salvándose
articles.summary: La temporada 2007-2008 empezó igual, perdió en la séptima jornada, cambió de entrenador en febrero y acabó salvándose
articles.body: En las 21 temporadas del Alba en Segunda división desde el cambio de siglo, los manchegos han conocido arranques de temporada de muy distinta naturaleza y algunos tan preocupantes como el actual. Estos días se ha recordado aquel inicio de la campaña 2007-08, en la que el conjunto que dirigía Quique Hernández comenzó perdiendo ante el Elche, empató en la segunda jornada ante el Xerez y encadenó cuatro derrotas frente a Hércules, Numancia, Sporting y Racing Ferrol. Tras seis partidos, un calco de la situación actual: un empate, cinco derrotas y un único punto en el casillero. Pero la historia no terminó allí. El equipo continuó sin ganar en la séptima jornada (derrota ante la Real Sociedad) y se plantó con 1/21 puntos tras ese primer tramo del campeonato. Quique Hernández continuó en el cargo hasta la Jornada 26, cuando Máximo Hernández le relevó. El nuevo técnico cerró la temporada con un balance de siete victorias, seis empates y tres derrotas en sus 16 partidos, y el Alba terminó 12º. Mal también empezó la temporada 2025-26, con Alberto González al frente: dos empates en los cinco primeros partidos y un panorama que invitaba al pesimismo. Sin embargo, el equipo acabó salvando la categoría con solvencia. Un escenario similar (1/15 puntos) ya se había vivido en la campaña 2017-18, con José Manuel Aira en el banquillo. Entonces, la temporada terminó con Enrique Martín relevando al berciano en la octava jornada y salvando al equipo en un último partido de infarto en Tenerife. Peor terminó la temporada 2020-21 con el mismo inicio, la destitución de Lucas Alcaraz en la quinta jornada, tres entrenadores más durante la temporada y un descenso traumático. Pese a todo, uno de los arranques más llamativos fue el de la temporada 2014-15, con Luis César Sampedro al frente: una victoria, dos empates y ocho derrotas (siete de ellas consecutivas entre las jornadas 5 y 11) y, pese a ello, el club mantuvo al técnico gallego en el cargo. El equipo logró reaccionar y salvó la categoría, finalizando en 14ª posición. Los precedentes sugieren que un mal inicio no necesariamente es sinónimo de desastre y, de hecho, el Alba de Alberto González ha demostrado tener una capacidad de resiliencia notable, capaz de navegar en la tormenta y llevar la nave a buen puerto cuando peor estaban las cosas. Ahora le llega, sin quererlo, una nueva oportunidad para demostrarlo. Para ello, una victoria en Girona el próximo viernes se antoja no sólo deseable, sino imprescindible. El Alba ha confirmado las lesiones de Javi Moreno y Lorenzo Aguado, a los que pierde para varias jornadas. Javi Moreno, sustituido durante la segunda parte del partido ante el Córdoba, sufre una lesión en su rodilla izquierda y tendrá que someterse a una artroscopia. Por su parte, Lorenzo Aguado también se perderá varios partidos debido a una lesión en los isquiotibiales de su pierna izquierda producida ante el conjunto cordobés. El parte de los servicios médicos del conjunto manchego no especifica tiempo de recuperación estimado para ninguno de los dos. Ambos futbolistas se unen a una larga lista de futbolistas con los que no puede contar Alberto González: Puertas, Obeng, Capi, San Bartolomé, Pepe Sánchez, Vallejo, Munir y Rober González, si bien los dos últimos pueden ser la gran novedad en la convocatoria para Girona.

articles.title: Alabama OC Ryan Grubb apologizes for blasting booing fans during Florida State game
articles.summary: The Alabama football team overcame a slow start to defeat Florida State in a recent game. Following that contest, Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb cr...
articles.body:
The Alabama football team overcame a slow start to defeat Florida State in a recent game. Following that contest, Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb criticized some fans who were booing the team. Grubb is now apologizing for those comments, per ESPN.

"My passion for The University of Alabama football team runs deep…my commitment to this program is rivaled only by my brothers who I lock arms with every day," Grubb wrote on social media, which was reported by ESPN. "I will always back my players…always. I normally speak very directly and don't cut words. That said — I should have worded my statement today more carefully. This is a special place with an incredible fanbase that all of us are thankful for. I have been spoiled by our great fans who are a sense of inspiration for our players. I let my loyalty and passion for my players affect my choice of words and offend some people that I certainly would have never intended to — the Crimson Tide faithful — and for that I apologize. I look forward to moving on and giving everyone something to cheer about! It's a blessing to be here at Alabama. I truly appreciate everyone and am looking forward to a great Saturday. Again, my sincere apologies…and ROLL TIDE!!!"

Alabama is now 3-0 on the season. The Crimson Tide fell behind against the Seminoles , before rallying to a 50-36 win.

The Crimson Tide's head coach Kalen DeBoer thinks his team has a lot to work on, after the Florida State game. Alabama football has aspirations this season to reach the College Football Playoff.

"You've got to be sharp," DeBoer said. "You've got to be locked in. Can't have the foolish penalty or just the lack of execution. You know, get your pads on a guy and finish the block. You know, go out there and have the physicality that we showed the last 2½ quarters."

articles.title: Rooney ya veía venir lo de JJ Gabriel: "Es un jugador de primera"
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolistas sabía que la situación de la perla del Manchester United sucedería en cualquier momento
articles.summary: El exfutbolistas sabía que la situación de la perla del Manchester United sucedería en cualquier momento
articles.body: La situación de JJ Gabriel en el Manchester United está en el aire. El joven de 15 años ha pedido salir del club, que ha intentado retenerlo a toda costa, y ahora los grandes clubes de Europa quieren incorporarlo a sus filas. Una joven perla que busca dar un salto en su carrera. Y una persona muy ligada a la entidad de Mánchester tenía claro que esto iba a acabar sucediendo. Se trata de Wayne Rooney, el mítico futbolista que conquistó Old Trafford. El exjugador ha tratado de cerca con JJ Gabriel, ya que forma parte del mismo equipo que su hijo. "He visto crecer a JJ, ha estado en el equipo de Kai. Cualquiera que estuviera cerca sabía que eso iba a pasar. No estoy seguro de que sea un fanático del Manchester United. Y creo que ha habido desde que tenía 12 o 13 años conversación de ir a jugar a España. Creo que para cualquiera que ha estado cerca de eso, no es una sorpresa en absoluto que esto haya sucedido", afirmó a Stick To United en Disney+. A pesar de los deseos del joven por salir, el Manchester United ha intentado por todos los medios evitar su salida. "Para ser justos con el Manchester United, han hecho todo, absolutamente todo, para retenerlo en el club. Probablemente lo han tratado de manera diferente a los demás jugadores porque es un jugador muy especial. Lo sé, lo reconozco, porque yo era ese tipo de jugador en el Everton. Yo recibía ese trato en el Everton", dijo "Es decepcionante porque es un jugador de primer nivel y un chico encantador. Nunca se sabe si la situación ha llegado demasiado lejos o si existe la posibilidad de que se quede", comentó Rooney. El siguiente paso en su carrera es llegar a la élite y demostrar de que está hecho. "Es un jugador de primera. Su habilidad, su equilibrio... ha demostrado que puede jugar en categorías superiores y marcar goles. El siguiente paso es el fútbol de primera división, donde todo es diferente, y nunca se sabe hasta que uno está ahí. Pero es un talento muy especial que entiende el juego a la perfección. En algún momento de esta temporada habría debutado con el primer equipo, supongo, así que ahí radica la decepción", añadió el exfutbolista. Y para Rooney, es un error intentar mantener a un futbolista que no quiere estar en el equipo. "Sin importar la edad, si no quieres estar en el club, no deberías mantener a los jugadores del club que no quieren estar allí, porque creo que envía un mensaje equivocado a los otros jugadores que quieren estar allí", sentenció.

articles.title: Apoteosis de la selección
articles.standfirst: Locura en Las Rozas en el primer entrenamiento de la campeona del mundo
articles.summary: Locura en Las Rozas en el primer entrenamiento de la campeona del mundo
articles.body: Dos estrellas por todos lados. Es la nueva realidad de la selección española, el equipo que es, como en 2010, a la vez campeón de Europa y del mundo. La selección vuelve a ponerse en marcha en su Ciudad Deportiva de Las Rozas en una tarde de fiesta nacional absoluta. Una apoteosis en rojo y gualda, y blanco, porque esa camiseta es un fenómeno comercial nunca antes visto, que comienza desde primera hora de la mañana. Desde muchas horas antes de que se abran las puertas de la Ciudad del Fútbol, decenas de aficionados se agolpan bajo un sol castigador a la espera del primer entrenamiento a puerta abierta de los campeones del mundo. El paso de las horas y el calor también provocaron algún momento de tensión para mantener la posición en la cola. Porque fueron muchas las personas que se quedaron sin entrar, a la espera de una posible orden de apertura de puertas. "Es que no podemos", contestaba uno de los miembros del equipo de seguridad a los ruegos de quienes estaban fuera para que tuviera piedad de ellos. Pero la seguridad estaba por encima de todo. Con una estrella o dos, lo que no cambia es que la camiseta de Lamine Yamal es la que más se ve entre los aficionados españoles. Algo que también sucede fuera de nuestras fronteras. El 19 de España es un fenómeno mundial multiplicado después de unir el Mundial en su primer intento a la Eurocopa, ganada también en su primera aparición en la competición. Aclamados todos y cada uno de los 26 jugadores convocados por De la Fuente, al igual que el seleccionador, Ferran es otro de los grandes focos de la algarabía de los aficionados. Su nombre se coreba ya antes de que los jugadores salieran al al camo. El ahora delantero del PSG es quien mandó la pelota a las redes del Dibu Martínez para convertir a España en bicampeona del mundo. Su nombre queda unido al de Iniesta en el corazón del fútbol español. Y eso se deja notar en el entusiasmo del cerca de dos millares de espectadores que acompañan a España en su regreso. El límite del aforo. Pasadas las siete de la tarde, los campeones del mundo, 21, y las cinco novedades, Josep Martínez, Fresneda, Huijsen, Fermín y Roberto Fernández, saltaron al campo principal de Las Rozas. Un clamor se apoderó de la grada. Es el sonido del agradecimiento al equipo que domina el mundo. A partir de ahí la locura no hizo más que aumentar. Estaba claro que el entrenamiento a puerta abierta se iba a convertir en una explosión de felicidad. El cántico de "campeones del mundo" fue el primero que sonó en la grada. Antes, los jugadores formaron un pasillo para festejar la renovación de todo el cuerpo técnico. La ración de collejas a De la Fuente y su staff fue considerable. Con la grada en modo fiesta, sobre el campo trabajaban 25 de los 26 jugadores convocados por De la Fuente. El único que se quedó en manos de los fisios fue Marc Pubill. Salió con todos, pero se volvió al vestuario a causa de unas ampollas en los pies. Nada relevante. Tanto que antes de acabar la sesión regresó al césped. El nombre de los jugadores coreados se fue sucediendo: Lamine, Ferran, Pedri, Cucurella, De la Fuente... Nadie en la grada pensaba en Inglaterra, Croacia y República Checa, los tres rivales de España en la Nations. Era una tarde de fiesta, de presumir de las dos estrellas, de cantar sin parar "campeones del mundo". La traca quedaba para el final. Tras apenas una hora de entrenamiento, De la Fuente mandó a los jugadores a la ducha. Llegaba el momento de los autógrafos, del contacto directo de los campeones con la gente. Y el éxtasis se apoderó de todo. El primero en acercarse a firmar fue Laporte. Después Mikel Merino. Y el griterío se convirtió en clamor cuando Rodri tomó el camino a la grada. Tras él, Ferran, Lamine, Pedri, Cucurella, Baena, Cubarsí... Pasión roja.

articles.title: Tiempo de Revisión señala a Ortiz Arias y a Trujillo Suárez: "Era roja a Kang-in Lee por la falta a Valverde"
articles.standfirst: El CTA corrige al colegiado madrileño por su error en el derbi del Metropolitano
articles.summary: El CTA corrige al colegiado madrileño por su error en el derbi del Metropolitano
articles.body: La actuación de Ortiz Arias y Trujillo Suárez en el derbi madrileño ya tiene respuesta por parte de sus 'jefes'. El CTA reconoce el error del colegiado de campo y el de VAR en la entrada de Kang-in Lee sobre Fede Valverde y señala que el jugador surcoreano debió ser expulsado con roja directa. "Tiro libre directo y roja directa", es la interpretación del CTA sobre la acción, que sentencia los dos errores: "Error claro y manifiesto del árbitro" y "El VAR debió intervenir". Respecto a la jugada entre Cuti Romero y Jude Bellingham, el CTA da por buena la actuación del dúo arbitral y explica por qué Ortiz Arias acude al monitor a revisar la acción. El colegiado, en un primer momento, amonesta al centrocampista del Real Madrid. Desde el VAR, al revisar la jugada, entienden que hay una confusión de identidad a la hora de sacar la tarjeta amarilla, puesto que el madridista es quien recibe la patada. Por eso, pese a que en televisión se vio el cartel 'Tarjeta roja en revisión', lo que realmente estaba haciendo Ortiz Arias era revertir la amarilla de Bellingham. Tras ver la acción, decide amonestar además al Cuti Romero. El Real Madrid pedía en esa jugada la tarjeta roja para el defensa argentino del Atlético de Madrid, pero el CTA dice que la jugada es de "intensidad con alta carga interpretativa" y que Ortiz Arias evalúa el pisotón como "temerario". El tercero de los errores que el CTA le achaca a Ortiz Arias en el derbi tiene lugar en el penalti de Huijsen sobre Giuliano, aunque aplaude la intervención del VAR a la hora de llamar al colegiado para cambiar su decisión. El árbitro, en un primer momento, pita penalti y saca amarilla al central del Real Madrid, pero desde la sala VOR le llaman para que revise la acción por si la infracción de Huijsen, en zona DOGSO, es merecedora de cartulina roja. Ortiz Arias va al monitor y decide entonces expulsar al madridista.

articles.title: Última semana de campaña por el Balón de Oro: los lectores de MARCA eligen a su ganador
articles.standfirst: El lunes 28 de septiembre se cierra el plazo para enviar los votos
articles.summary: El lunes 28 de septiembre se cierra el plazo para enviar los votos
articles.body: El próximo lunes 26 de octubre, el teatro London Palladium acogerá la gala del Balón de Oro, la edición más abierta de los últimos años, con varios candidatos y ningún favorito claro. El 70 aniversario del galardón se presenta más interesante que nunca y, ante la ausencia de un favoritísimo, aquellos aspirantes que se ven con opciones apuran una campaña a la que le queda una semana. El 28 de septiembre acaba el plazo para que se envíen los votos y, entonces, será el momento de recontar. Es la última semana también para que los lectores de MARCA elijan a su ganador del Balón de Oro. Los últimos días para depositar el voto en una encuesta que, tras la gala, servirá de comparación con la lista definitiva. Los grandes candidatos no quieren dejar ningún cabo suelto y se han pasado las últimas semanas dejando claro que ellos creen que deberían ganar el trofeo. "Sería una decepción no ganar el Balón de Oro, no hubo nadie mejor que yo la temporada pasada", es la última frase de un Mbappé que lleva varios días insistiendo en sus posibilidades. También Lamine quiere ser considerado principal candidato. "El Balón de Oro premia al jugador excepcional, no tiene que ver con la cantidad de goles", ha dicho el delantero del Barcelona en clara alusión a sus dos grandes competidores, Mbappé y Harry Kane. A los goles aludió el delantero inglés en su entrevista con MARCA para dar valor a lo hecho la temporada pasada: "No me gusta hablar de mí, los 73 goles hablan por sí solos". La selección española, campeona del mundo, cuenta con una amplia representación. Lamine Yamal, Rodri Hernández, Fabián Ruiz, Ferran Torres, Marc Cucurella y Pau Cubarsí forman parte de una lista en la que también destaca el peso del PSG campeón de Europa. El conjunto parisino aporta al propio Fabián, Ousmane Dembélé, Vitinha, William Pacho, Marquinhos, Joao Neves, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Nuno Mendes y Achraf Hakimi, además de Ferran, (recién fichado en el mercado estival) todos ellos protagonistas de la campaña que llevó al equipo francés a volver conquistar la Champions. Pero el abanico de candidatos no termina ahí. Kylian Mbappé, Michael Olise, Harry Kane y Lionel Messi (vuelve a estar nominado tras tres ediciones de ausencia) también figuran entre los grandes nombres de una lista a la que llegan después de firmar grandes campañas

articles.title: ¿Qué se sabe de Go Sports?: El nuevo canal que transmitiría el fútbol colombiano desde 2027
articles.standfirst: Mauricio Correa está detrás del canal internacional que quiere transmitir la Liga BetPlay en 2027
articles.summary: Mauricio Correa está detrás del canal internacional que quiere transmitir la Liga BetPlay en 2027
articles.body: La puja por los derechos de transmisión del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano ha entrado en una fase decisiva tras la asamblea de la Dimayor del pasado 21 de septiembre de 2026. La sorpresiva irrupción de Go Sports, una firma registrada en Panamá, se perfila como la principal contendiente para desbancar a Win Sports a partir de 2027. Sin embargo, su propuesta económica viene acompañada de cuestionamientos sobre su estructura operativa y la figura del empresario Mauricio Correa. Go Sports presentó una oferta cercana a los 90 millones de dólares por un contrato de 7 años para adquirir los derechos de televisión del FPC, con la opción de sublicenciarlos. La propuesta contempla un esquema de alianza estratégica junto a la productora Mediapro y un fondo de inversión árabe. Ante este escenario, Win Sports, actual tenedor de los derechos, cuenta con un plazo de 60 días hábiles para igualar o superar la oferta si desea mantener la exclusividad del torneo local, al no registrarse otras propuestas durante la asamblea. Pese a figurar con sede administrativa en Bogotá, las investigaciones periodísticas lideradas por Alejandro Pino Calad señalan que Go Sports Media fue fundada en Panamá el 26 de noviembre de 2012 y carece de capacidad instalada o infraestructura de producción propia en Colombia. El vínculo entre la Dimayor y la firma panameña data de más de una década. A través de cláusulas contractuales, Go Sports ha percibido un porcentaje recurrente de las licencias del FPC, superando en rendimientos consolidados a clubes tradicionales como Atlético Nacional, Millonarios o América de Cali. La figura central en torno a Go Sports es el dirigente Mauricio Correa, un actor histórico en la comercialización del fútbol televisado en Colombia. Fundó el canal FPC en Telmex a mediados de los 2000. En 2012 estructuró el lanzamiento de Win Sports junto a directivos de la Dimayor. Tras salir de la dirección de Win en 2018, estuvo al frente de proyectos de producción continental y la implementación del VAR en Colombia con Mediapro. Aunque Correa ha buscado desmarcarse públicamente de la propiedad legal de Go Sports alegando la reserva de la sociedad anónima en Panamá, diversos analistas y periodistas cuestionan su rol, señalando que ejerce como defensor activo de los contratos comerciales de la firma.

articles.title: Celtic report £4.8m loss as revenue drops by 22.7%
articles.summary: Celtic announce a loss after tax of £4.8m for the year ending June 30, 12 months on from making a profit of £33.9m.
articles.body:
Celtic have announced a loss after tax of £4.8m for the year ending June 30, 12 months on from making a profit of £33.9m.

The club say the shift is largely due to the failure to secure Champions League participation last season.

The figures show revenue down by 22.7% to £111m (£143.6m in 2025), with the Scottish Premiership leaders reporting a cash in the bank total of £66.4m.

Celtic had three different managers in 2025-26, with Brendan Rodgers departing and Wilfried Nancy fired after an eight-game reign, while chairman Peter Lawwell retired in December, citing "abuse and threats".

Describing the campaign as "more turbulent than anyone would have wished for", interim chairman Brian Wilson went on to congratulate Martin O'Neill and staff for "demonstrating extraordinary resilience" to deliver a league and Scottish Cup double.

Wilson went on to say that Celtic spent £31.6m this summer to recruit Kasper Hogh, Camilo Duran, Mika Baur, Haissem Hassan, Joel van den Berg and Jordan Lotomba, while loan deals were done for Landon Emenalo, Shumaira Mheuka, Sam Johnstone and Oliver Sorensen.

He did not reveal how much had been made from the sale of players, including Daizen Maeda, Arne Engels and Reo Hatate.

Celtic are again in the Europa League this term after a shock capitulation away to LASK in the Champions League play-off.

They are out of the League Cup and their Premiership lead has been cut to two points following back-to-back defeats by Rangers.

"The events of the past 12 months have been dramatic, sometimes joyful and at other points deeply frustrating," added Wilson.

"The departure of Brendan Rodgers was an unanticipated event which initiated a period of instability. In other circumstances, the appointment of Wilfried Nancy might have worked but his arrival in mid-season and the changes which followed clearly did not.

"Parting ways with Wilfried was hugely disappointing but decisive action had to be taken. The return of the great Martin O'Neill, supported by his backroom team as well as a fine squad of players, then proved to be a triumphant success."

Wilson referenced the need to improve "communication and supporter engagement", saying that work was "ongoing", adding that the search continues for a permanent chairman.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta contract: Arsenal boss agrees new deal to extend stay at Premier League champions
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has agreed to a new deal at Arsenal; Arteta had entered the final year of his current contract at the club but now extends his stay at the Emirates Stadium; the 44-year-old is already the longest-serving manager in England's top-four leagues after his appointment in 2019
articles.body:
The 44-year-old's existing contract with the Premier League champions, signed in September 2024, was due to expire next summer.

But the Spaniard, who was appointed in 2019, has committed his future to the club and confirmation of his new agreement is expected during this international break.

When asked about his contract situation ahead of Arsenal's trip to Brighton on Saturday, Arteta said: "I think we are all very much aligned; whenever the time is right, we'll get that done. There is nothing to be concerned about.

"I think we both have the same ambition and the same will. So whenever we have time, we'll get that resolved."

Arteta has transformed Arsenal's fortunes during his tenure and guided the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season following three straight second-place finishes.

He also led the Gunners to only their second Champions League final, which they lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain. He has previously won an FA Cup and three Community Shields.

'Arteta's new deal agreed but not signed'

Analysis by Sky Sports News' Gary Cotterill:

"It's not signed yet. Officially, the club are not saying it has been agreed, but our understanding is that an agreement has been in place for a couple of weeks.

"Mikel Arteta alluded to that on Friday when I asked him about it. He said they are aligned and in agreement.

"So, I believe the deal is agreed. It's now a case of sorting the formalities, sitting down and signing the contract.

"I expect that to happen during the next international break, potentially within the next two weeks.

"When he signed his current contract two years ago, that was also completed during the international break, on September 12.

"He tends to compartmentalise things. He has a break, then turns his attention to his future.

"The agreement has been in place for weeks. The only thing left now is to get the contract signed and make the announcement. The full details of the deal should follow in the coming weeks."

articles.title: Benjamín Noval vuela hacia el arcoíris y se proclama campeón del mundo júnior contrarreloj
articles.standfirst: El asturiano, de sólo 17 años, firma una actuación extraordinaria en Montreal y conquista la segunda medalla de España en este Mundial
articles.summary: El asturiano, de sólo 17 años, firma una actuación extraordinaria en Montreal y conquista la segunda medalla de España en este Mundial
articles.body: Benjamín Noval miró al cronómetro y esperó. Ya había hecho su parte: 20,3 kilómetros a toda velocidad por Montreal, una última subida exprimido hasta el límite y un tiempo de 25 minutos y 17 segundos. Pero todavía faltaba por llegar Vic de Smet. El belga cruzó la meta seis segundos después. Entonces Noval pudo soltar todo lo que llevaba dentro: era campeón del mundo júnior de contrarreloj. El oro puso fin a una espera que había comenzado un año antes, en Kigali. Allí, una caída en un momento decisivo le apartó de la pelea por el maillot arcoíris. La escena seguía acompañándolo al llegar a Canadá. "Aunque siga ahí, yo intento borrar la imagen", confesó a MARCA antes del Mundial. No necesitaba olvidar lo ocurrido para volver a intentarlo. Le bastaba con que aquella caída no decidiera también esta carrera. Noval salió con cautela en el sector más técnico. Las curvas exigían atención y el asturiano prefirió asegurar antes de abrir el acelerador. En el primer parcial pasó tercero, a tres segundos del mejor registro. La carrera estaba abierta y De Smet aparecía como una amenaza seria. Después llegó el terreno en el que Noval podía imponer su fuerza. En el segundo tramo cambió la prueba. El corredor de Pola de Laviana marcó el mejor parcial y abrió diez segundos respecto al belga. Ya no corría únicamente contra sus rivales: corría contra la posibilidad de que el esfuerzo se le hiciera eterno antes de la meta. Mantuvo la posición sobre la bicicleta, apretó los dientes en la subida final y detuvo el reloj con un tiempo que ninguno de los ocho corredores pendientes de terminar pudo mejorar. De Smet fue el último en acercarse. Recortó cuatro segundos en el desenlace, pero no los suficientes. Se quedó con la plata; el danés Malthe Risbjerg completó el podio, a 16 segundos de Noval. Para el español llegaron los abrazos con la selección y con su padre, también llamado Benjamín y antiguo ciclista profesional. "Aún no me lo creo, estoy asimilándolo todavía", reconoció el campeón después de la carrera. Explicó que había afrontado con prudencia el inicio para evitar una caída y que, al encontrar terreno favorable, había ido "a tope hasta la meta". Era el plan de alguien que conocía demasiado bien el precio de un error en un Mundial. El título supone la segunda medalla española en Montreal, después del bronce de Héctor Álvarez en la crono sub-23, y el primer oro de la delegación. Para Noval llega antes de dar el salto al primer equipo del Netcompany Ineos en 2027. El jueves tendrá otra oportunidad en la prueba en ruta. Hoy puede quedarse un momento más con esta imagen: la del arcoíris sobre sus hombros, ocupando por fin el lugar que hasta ahora tenía Kigali.

articles.title: Thierry Henry Lists NYC Penthouse for $25 Million, Property Was Purchased for $14.9M in 2010
articles.summary: World football legend Thierry Henry is putting his Manhattan penthouse on the market, and for the princely sum of $25 million it can be yours.
articles.body:
World football legend Thierry Henry is putting his Manhattan penthouse on the market, and for the princely sum of $25 million it can be yours.

The Wall Street Journal 's Libertina Brandt reported Tuesday that Henry is looking to cash in on the property he originally purchased for $14.9 million.

The former France international bought the penthouse in conjunction with his move to MLS' New York Red Bulls. Aside from a brief lone spell with Arsenal, he spent his final five professional seasons in the United States.

Henry is one of the greatest players of his generation. He won two Premier League titles with Arsenal and scored 175 goals in 258 appearances. The 49-year-old went on to lift a pair of La Liga titles and a Champions League trophy with Barcelona.

At the national team level, Henry won the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000 with Les Bleus.

For younger fans, the 2003 Ballon d'Or runner-up is known more for his work in the studio than on the pitch. He has played a starring role alongside Kate Scott, Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards in CBS Sports' coverage of the Champions League.

articles.title: Micheal Martin: Israel FA comments on Heimir Hallgrimsson 'unacceptable'
articles.summary: Irish taoiseach Micheal Martin says comments made by the Israel Football Association about the Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson are "unacceptable".
articles.body:
Irish taoiseach [prime minister] Micheal Martin said comments made by the Israel Football Association about the Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson are "unacceptable" and "should be withdrawn".

Israel's football governing body accused Hallgrimmson of "ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity" regarding comments made last week when he said: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The teams are set to meet twice in the space of a week in the Nations League, with Israel's 'home' game in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday, with the return fixture also in a neutral venue of Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October.

On Monday, the Israel FA posted a message on X, saying: "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way.

"Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach.

"We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, We're playing against the coach who embodies them."

While the Football Association of Ireland [FAI] did not respond, Martin did comment.

"They are unacceptable remarks and should be withdrawn," he told reporters in New York, where he is attending the UN General Assembly.

"We're very clear and I think [UN secretary-general] Antonio Guterres said it again this morning, he has never in his lifetime seen the level and scale of death and destruction as he witnessed in terms of the Israeli government's war on Gaza in the aftermath of the horrific Hamas attack preceding the war. Our manager is saying the exact same thing.

"Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious

Uefa rejected request to keep Republic of Ireland and Israel separate - FAI

There have been increasing calls in Ireland for a boycott of the fixtures, with a protest held at the Republic of Ireland team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

This followed an open letter by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, signed by over 160 Irish sportspeople, urging the FAI to withdraw from the fixtures because of the situation in Gaza.

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel has repeatedly denied that it has committed genocide, as well as war crimes and crimes against humanity. It says its military operations in Gaza have been conducted in self-defence and in accordance with international law.

articles.title: Celtic: Martin O'Neill backed by chief executive Michael Nicholson despite 'painful' week
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill revealed he was going to reflect on his future after three defeats in a week, two of which came against Rangers in the League Cup and Scottish Premiership; Celtic also lost their Europa League opener, less than a month after their Champions League play-off collapse
articles.body:
The Parkhead club lost twice to Rangers - in the League Cup quarter-finals and Scottish Premiership - plus at home to Ferencvaros in their Europa League opener.

It follows last month's collapse against LASK in their Champions League play-off , losing the tie on aggregate despite leading 4-0 at one stage.

Following the second of those Old Firm defeats, O'Neill said he was going to reflect on his future and admitted "it might be time to wrap it up".

While Nicholson has admitted "the losses in the last week have been painful for us all", he insists the club "will now come together and support Martin and the players, as we focus our efforts on achieving success domestically and in the Europa League."

O'Neill's return to Celtic last October - 20 years after his first spell as manager - came following the resignation of Brendan Rodgers.

Another spell as interim boss followed weeks later as Wilfried Nancy was sacked after a dismal 33-day tenure.

Nicholson added that the club "owe a debt of gratitude" to O'Neill and his management team for stepping in twice last season, and says the club were "delighted" he agreed to return on a permanent basis this summer.

Celtic loss revealed amid transfer revelation

The Celtic board have faced criticism from supporters over its recruitment strategy.

Figures in the report reveal £31.7m was spent on the likes of record signing Kasper Hogh, plus Camilo Duran, Mika Baur, Haïssem Hassan and others, with Nicholson adding the club worked with O'Neill over transfers.

However, that period is not covered in the report that highlights a post-tax loss of £4.8m, a stark contrast to the £33.9m profit 12 months prior.

Chairman Brian Wilson's statement highlighted a lack of Champions League football, increased wages and a smaller profit in player trading as some of the reasons why.

Celtic did end the year until June 2026 with £66.4m in the bank.

Celtic 'feeling the pinch' for struggles in Europe

Analysis by Sky Sports News' Anthony Joseph:

Celtic's lack of preparation for Champions League qualifiers has been laid bare today - and it's costing the club around £40m dropping into the Europa League.

The club released their financial results tonight for the year ending on June 30 - revealing a £4.8m loss after a £33.9m profit in the previous year.

They reached the knockout play-offs in European competition in both seasons, so what was the difference? The answer was the competition itself: the previous season was in the Champions League, while last season was in the Europa League.

Celtic's revenue for the 2024/2025 season was £143.6m. Around £75m was from their exploits in the new format of the Champions League, which they had entered automatically from winning the title.

Due to Scotland's decreasing coefficient, the Hoops - then led by Brendan Rodgers - had to negotiate a play-off to get into the Champions League last season, which they lost on penalties to Kairat Almaty.

Rodgers had spoken multiple times about needing to invest in the squad before the qualifiers, but Celtic went into the tie still without replacements for Kyogo Furuhashi (who was sold to Rennes in January 2025 for £10m) and Nicolas Kuhn, who they sold to Como that summer for £16.5m.

The failure to prepare and qualify for the Champions League led to one of most chaotic seasons in Celtic's recent history.

The fans launched a campaign to boycott merchandise and kiosk spending at Celtic Park, while Rodgers eventually resigned over what he believed was the club's lack of ambition in the transfer window. Former manager Martin O'Neill, 74, came out of punditry to take charge until Wilfried Nancy was appointed in December, only for O'Neill to return 33 days after Nancy was sacked.

Celtic did go on to win the double in the most dramatic of ways and they got to the knockouts of the Europa League. But revenue was down 22.7 per cent to £111m, with the club making an overall loss last term.

Fans had hoped to see a change from the board in how they approached this season's Champions League play-off.

It can be argued that the club were more prepared - having spent around £32m on record-signing Kasper Høgh, Camilo Duran, Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan. However, they sold Arne Engels for £22m to West Ham just before the tie with LASK Linz, with no replacement brought in - something that irked O'Neill.

Being 4-0 up on aggregate with 57 minutes to go in Austria, Celtic should never have collapsed like they did to miss out on the Champions League. But for them to finish that tie with the likes of Anthony Ralston, Luke McCowan and Dane Murray suggests the squad was lacking depth to be ready for a game of such magnitude.

And that will leave yet another £40m black hole in next year's results, unless the club go far in this year's Europa League.

But it begs the question as to why the club, who are sitting on £66m of cash in the bank, don't fully prepare themselves for these qualifiers and show more ambition to treat Europe as a major priority. Even financially, it makes more sense.

For every £100 you earn in the Champions League, you only get £22 in the Europa League according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire.

And Celtic are certainly feeling that pinch now.

articles.title: Martin O'Neill: Manager backed by Celtic after 'painful' week
articles.summary: Celtic will "come together and support" manager Martin O'Neill after a "painful" week for the club, says chief executive Michael Nicholson.
articles.body:
Celtic will "come together and support" manager Martin O'Neill after a "painful" week for the club, chief executive Michael Nicholson has said.

O'Neill had indicated that he would use the international break to consider his future following two defeats to Rangers, either side of a home loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

In the wake of Sunday's 1-0 derby defeat at Celtic Park, 74-year-old O'Neill had said "it might be time to wrap it up".

However, Nicholson suggested the club will rally round the manager who has delivered nine trophies over two spells.

His remarks came with the latest financial figures revealing a drop of nearly £33m in revenue.

A loss of £4.8m is largely down to the failure to reach last year's Champions League and Celtic have missed out again, squandering a 4-0 aggregate lead in their play-off with LASK last month.

"Having started well in the Premiership this season, we experienced disappointment in the Champions League play-off," said Nicholson in a written statement accompanying the financial results.

"Reaching the league phase of the Champions League is an objective for us all, and we are sorry not to have achieved it.

"On top of that, the losses in the last week have been painful for us all. We will now come together and support Martin and the players, as we focus our efforts on achieving success domestically and in the Europa League."

articles.title: Women's Champions League: Arsenal win with late penalty; Man City rescue draw at Bayern Munich
articles.summary: Mariona Caldentey's stoppage-time penalty secured a 1-0 win for Arsenal against KB HB Koge; Man City come from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 at Bayern Munich as goals from Beth Mead and Carlotta Wamser ensure City do not lose on their European return.
articles.body:
There were wholesale changes for Gunners boss Renee Slegers, who inserted eight different faces into her starting line-up from Sunday's 1-1 Women's Super League draw with Manchester United.

Chloe Kelly had the ball in the back of the net in the first half, but the England forward's would-be opener was disallowed following a VAR check.

Arsenal, who had lacked end product throughout, were gifted an opportunity when Selina Cerci was brought down and substitute Caldentey secured all three points with a bottom-corner finish.

Greek referee Eleni Antoniu was called to the monitor after Kelly beat Alberte Vingum in the 12th minute, but it was chalked off after it was determined Stina Blackstenius had been offside in the build-up.

Maanum drew another save in the 25th minute, with the game rarely venturing outside the visitors' half until Macy Schultz's deflected effort drifted towards the crossbar.

There was a cross-shot from Maanum, who could not connect with a team-mate, before a Kyra Cooney-Cross effort also drifted wide.

Blackstenius was replaced by Alessia Russo after the break and there were a couple of Arsenal chances in quick succession in what started as a more end-to-end opening to the second half, including a Smilla Holmberg free-kick punched away by Vingum.

The clinical finish, though, still evaded Arsenal, who wasted a handful of set-pieces and watched as Maanum directed an effort over the bar.

Holmberg prevented danger with an alert clearance after Emelia Oskarsdottir's cross fell loose, then came within a couple of inches as her corner caught the crossbar directly.

Then, in the third of four minutes of stoppage time, Yukina Sakabe sent Cerci tumbling. Antoniou pointed to the spot, and Caldentey buried the ball past Vingum.

Man City fight back from two down to draw at Bayern

Manchester City's eventful return to the Women's Champions League saw them come from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 away to Bayern Munich and become the first English side to avoid defeat to the Germans in Europe.

City's Germany international Carlotta Wamser was left completely unmarked in the penalty area to score her first City goal in the 86th minute after prolific striker Khadija "Bunny" Shaw had earlier missed a penalty to equalise.

The visitors were worthy of a point based on their second-half performance, having been completely dominated before the interval before nicking a goal on the stroke of half-time.

Bayern were 2-0 up inside the first half-hour and had chances to put the result beyond doubt, but with seconds ticking down to the interval Kerstin Casparij's break down the right led to Beth Mead eventually tapping in.

However, the hosts were unhappy that play had been allowed to continue, with a flare thrown onto the pitch as the attack developed. Casparij had crossed the ball before reaching the thick blue cloud, though, and the goal was allowed to stand.

It was the stroke of luck City needed, and they benefited again when Ena Mahmutovic appeared caught between two minds as she raced out to close down Aoba Fujino.

The goalkeeper initially appeared content to let the ball run out of play, only to inexplicably stick out a leg and bring down the City winger.

Shaw, who had been due to be substituted, could not capitalise and was immediately replaced. Wamser, however, ensured the miss did not prove costly.

City were fortunate to have only a two-goal deficit to overturn, with Klara Buhl and Pernille Harder both going close before Giulia Gwinn's chipped effort across Ayaka Yamashita opened the scoring in the 11th minute.

Linda Dallmann had been allowed to drive unchallenged from the halfway line before finding Gwinn, who calmly lifted the ball over Yamashita and into the far corner.

Buhl then volleyed straight at Yamashita, while Jovana Damjanović blazed over as Bayern cut through City's midfield once again.

Lauren Hemp almost conjured a goal out of nothing when her deflected cross clipped the top of the crossbar, but it proved only a brief respite.

Harder soon whipped a cross into the box, with Casparij making a complete mess of her attempted clearance and inadvertently diverting the ball into her own net.

Coffey 'proud' of draw and praises City's depth

Man City Women midfielder Sam Coffey told the club's official website:

"Beth's goal changed momentum going into half-time. We connected better and were more front-footed in the second half. So it was huge to take that into half-time and continue to turn the game around.

"We wanted to win the game, so we're disappointed we didn't do that, but to come away from a really tough place with a draw is something we should be proud of."

On the subs: "It's one of the best parts of our team of how deep we are. We have so many gamechangers and whoever comes into the game is going to have an impact on it.

"That's what the best teams in the world need and want, and I think we have that to the nth degree."

articles.title: Super League: Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors will be subject to an independent investigation into their conduct and actions over the past 12 months
articles.summary: Conduct of Leigh and Wigan to be investigated by the Rugby Football League (RFL) following high-profile ticketing saga; Leigh were beaten by Trinity in their eliminator match at the weekend
articles.body:
The Leopards and the Warriors have had an ongoing dispute for almost 12 months, dating back to the high-profile ticketing saga that led to Leigh's owner Derek Beaumont saying his club would not participate in the fixture over a disagreement about their ticket allocation of 4,800 .

They ultimately did play the game and were eliminated from the play-offs with Wigan winning 18-6.

With the Warriors set to host Wakefield in the play-off semi-final on Saturday, matters reignited again over the weekend after an original post from Wigan detailed ticketing arrangements for whichever side visited the Brick this weekend in the play-offs would receive an allocation of 5,000 tickets for safety reasons.

Leigh were beaten by Wakefield Trinity in their eliminator match , where a win for the Leopards would have seen them progress to face Wigan instead.

Beaumont put himself in the spotlight again with a tirade on social media site X following Wigan's statement and his activity could also breach the RFL's own social media code of conduct.

The RFL said in a statement: "The independent Rugby Football League and RL Commercial Boards have issued a letter to both Leigh Leopards RLFC and Wigan Warriors RLFC advising them there will be an independent investigation into the conduct and actions of both clubs and the governing body in relation to matters extending over the last 12 months.

"The RFL and RL Commercial will not make any further comment until the investigation is complete."

Wigan finished top of the Super League regular season table, while Leigh finished fifth.

articles.title: Morocco election: How Ceuta, football and Israel have shaped the campaign
articles.summary: Young voters are being courted with football slogans, promises of jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls.
articles.body:
Disillusioned young voters in Morocco were courted with viral football slogans, promises of one million jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls ahead of Wednesday's parliamentary elections.

Yet, for many young Moroccans, politics remains deeply disconnected from reality.

"I have no hope for this election. I'm ashamed of our political scene. It's a complete circus," Siham Azeroual, 32, an environmental activist who lives in the Atlas region, tells the BBC.

The outcome of the vote will decide the make-up of the next government, just weeks after 60,000 people risked their lives to cross from the North African country to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta - a sign of the lack of opportunities many young people feel they have at home.

Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy where political parties compete for 395 seats in the House of Representatives, the legislative chamber.

Yet executive power remains closely tied to the crown. King Mohammed VI, the 63-year-old monarch, appoints the prime minister from the political party that comes first in the election, but also presides over the Council of Ministers - the country's most important policy-making body.

The current campaign also follows a wave of Gen Z protests that erupted in September 2025 over unemployment, healthcare and living costs.

Demonstrators chanted slogans like "freedom, dignity, and social justice" which escalated to "get out Akhannouch", a reference to current Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch.

More than 2,400 people faced prosecution following the unrest. Despite the crackdown, some young activists are choosing to enter the political arena.

Hamza El Kharroubi, 29, was briefly arrested during the protests. He is now running for parliament with the little-known Environment and Sustainable Development Party, which has a green agenda.

"As a young person, I don't have much hope. I joined this party because they wanted more Gen Z faces and they are allowing us to speak freely about our demands," El Kharroubi tells the BBC.

He comes from Tetouan, just 34km (21 miles) from Fnideq beach, where the migration wave to Ceuta started in late July.

Some 60,000 people crossed, both Moroccans and other nationalities. At least 100 people died in the largest migration surge to the enclave in recent history.

"We want justice for the families of those who died crossing to Ceuta. We want compensation for their families," El Kharroubi says.

He argues that the crossing was widely linked to economic hardship and unemployment.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates overall unemployment stood at 13% last year, while youth unemployment - between the ages of 15 and 24 - reached 37.3%.

El Kharroubi says his goal is not to compete with established heavyweights - but securing a voice in parliament to build toward 2031.

"As young people, we have to enter the parliament so by 2031 we have strong young politicians who can compete for a seat in the government."

Fouzi Lekjaa, head of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation and a senior politician who works in the finance ministry, has emerged as the kingdom's newest political sensation - and a definite heavyweight.

Credited with helping the Atlas Lions - as the national men's football team is known - become global contenders, Lekjaa joined the centrist Party of Authenticity and Modernity (Pam) in July.

Videos of his campaign rallies have gone viral in the football-mad nation that is jointly hosting the next World Cup along with Spain and Portugal.

The clips show crowds chanting "Sir" which means "Go" in Moroccan Arabic - the iconic catchphrase from Morocco's historic 2022 World Cup run, when it became the first Arab and African side to make it to the semi-finals.

Lekjaa has promised to make Morocco sixth in the world in education and healthcare, to match the Fifa ranking of the men's football team.

Pam is competing against 26 other parties, including Prime Minister Akhannouch's National Rally of Independents (RNI). In its bid for a second term, RNI has renewed a pledge to create one million job opportunities by 2031.

Political expert Rachid Aourraz, from the Moroccan Institute for Policy Analysis (MIPA), remains sceptical about this promise.

"The slogan 'one million jobs' has become an overused electoral slogan. There is also talk of raising the minimum wage, but what is proposed cannot withstand a structural inability to create stable net jobs," Aourraz tells the BBC.

He adds that major parties "do not compete over an alternative model", but rather over how to implement public policies set by a royal vision.

Also seeking a political comeback is the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD) - using anti-Israeli sentiments to woo voters.

Morocco normalised ties with Israel in December 2020 along with several other Arab countries, under the US-brokered Abraham Accords.

Led by populist former Prime Minister Abdelilah Benkirane, the PJD is campaigning heavily on a promise to end diplomatic ties with Israel. He says the normalisation was a "mistake" made by his party which led the government between 2016 and 2021.

Bilateral ties were hit during the Gaza war with weekly protests taking place in the capital, Rabat, against the Israeli diplomatic presence.

During the conflict the Israeli liaison office was closed and direct flights between the two countries were suspended.

Yet despite an outpouring of pro-Palestinian protests, with tens of thousands taking to the streets and setting ablaze the Israeli flag at the height of the war, it was announced earlier this month that Israel and Morocco had agreed to open full embassies in their respective countries.

This followed a meeting between their top diplomats and the US ambassador to the United Nations.

"We have to speak up," Benkirane told supporters at a campaign rally in Marrakesh.

"If we work hard, the king will close the Israeli embassy. The king does not like going against his own people," he added, warning of "the dangers of Israel and Zionism in Morocco".

More than half of Morocco's total population of roughly 38.8 million is under the age of 35 - though only 4% of the more than 15.8 million registered voters are aged between 18 and 24.

"I am not keeping up much with the campaigns - but I noticed the same faces as usual," says Hiba, a 27-year-old Moroccan living in Canada who preferred not to use her last name.

She lives in Montreal which has a large Moroccan diaspora of about 104,000 people, according to the 2016 census.

Many of last year's Gen Z protests were more vocal outside the country, where young Moroccans were able to express their anger without fear of repercussions.

Hiba, who co-organised several Gen Z protests in Montreal, says she would have considered voting had she been able to find a proxy in Morocco - which is how those in the diaspora can cast their ballot.

"Gen Z protests didn't go in vain. We achieved something. At least now we see more debates with young people on state TV," she says.

Azeroual, the environmental activist, agrees.

But having lived through both the 20 February movement in 2011 that changed the constitution and the recent Gen Z movement, she believes change must come from a multi-faceted approach.

"I think young people should focus on the microscale - rather than running for office, helping build communities and connecting with people and then building up to the top," she says.

Despite not being fully convinced by any political campaign, she says she will be heading to her local polling station to cast her ballot.

articles.title: NY Giants Likely To Lose Jaxson Dart For 2026 Season: Why Signing Derek Carr May Be Only Hope of Playoff Appearance?
articles.summary: On Tuesday afternoon, the worst fears of New York Giants fans were realized with an updated diagnosis of Jaxson Dart’s […]
articles.body:
On Tuesday afternoon, the worst fears of New York Giants fans were realized with an updated diagnosis of Jaxson Dart's knee injury from Monday Night.

There was a ton of excitement among Giants fans heading into their Week 2 clash with Super Bowl favorites the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football . They were coming off a big season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys . Were being led by an elite coach who has given them a gritty and tough identity. And they seemed to have a budding star quarterback leading the offense.

Then it all seemed to go down the toilet in their first series when Dart's left leg was bent in a gruesome fashion that put a pit in the stomach of Big Blue fans. While he walked off on his own power and was seen standing around on the sidelines in street clothes, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafol broke the news that the QB's " knee injury is more severe than initially anticipated, and he could miss the rest of the season ."

The news is a nasty blow to a season that had emerging playoff hopes just a few days ago. Now the team will hand the keys of the offense to journeyman Jameis Winston . And as Giants fans saw last night, the No. 1 overall pick in 2105 NFL Draft won't be able to guide this team to a playoff appearance if he is the QB1 for the rest of the campaign.

So the Giants are left with two options. Let the season play out and consider replacing the oft-injured Dart with a star from a deep QB draft class next year, or try to salvage the season by adding a veteran QB.

Chances are they will try to find another signal caller on the trade or free agent market in the weeks ahead. But which one would be a realistic option to land, and who could actually guide them to the playoffs this season?

Why Derek Carr might be the perfect NY Giants replacement option for Jaxson Dart

The timing of Dart's injury brings added frustration because going into Week 3 means few teams are open to making moves. Furthermore, the Giants are desperate, so they have no leverage in a potential deal.

Veterans like Joe Flacco , Anthony Richardson Sr., Kenny Pickett , and Mac Jones all would be intriguing options to replace Dart. However, at this point in the season, the asking price may be too high. That's why the free agent market will offer the best option, and the top player available is former Las Vegas Raiders star Derek Carr .

Carr created headlines in the offseason when he suggested he'd be open to ending his retirement to get the chance to start for a playoff contender. Well, that opportunity may now be available. If the four-time Pro Bowler is fully recovered from his shoulder issues, is given time to get back into football shape and learn their system, then he has the talent to lead them to the playoffs.

Furthermore, to be coached by John Harbaugh and play with a roster that is good enough to make a run at a playoff spot, Carr may be willing to take a team-friendly contract if he is assured he will be the starter when ready.

While injuries were a problem for him in the final years of his career, he still posted a 14-13 record with the New Orleans Saints , a completion percentage of 68.0, a passer rating of 99.4 and 30 touchdowns to 13 interceptions. QB numbers that can be good for a team that has talent to keep them in the playoff hunt for the rest of the season.
